A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SA-ResGS. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, uncertainty-calibration results, component ablations, robustness tests, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds backbone experiments, controlled ablations, baseline comparisons, and scene-wise ablation statistics.

M1.justification: The default MASt3R triangulation, coverage prefiltering, FisherRF selection, and residual losses remain. The optional pi3/ICP alternative in v1 is replaced by a DA-v3 implementation using joint lifting with eight extrapolated views, confidence filtering, and Umeyama alignment (v3 Appendix A.5). This changes an alternative implementation without redesigning the core framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same reconstruction and uncertainty tasks on NeRF Synthetic, Mip-NeRF 360, and indoor/outdoor scenes from Deep Blending and Tanks and Temples. The seven-to-five-scene revision changes sampling within retained benchmark coverage, assessed under E3; the added backbone and ablation configurations do not introduce distinct task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates Nerfacto plus BayesRays and 3DGS plus ActiveNeRF in Table S9. It also compares random, farthest-view, MUSIQ, and CrossScore prefilters under a common FisherRF final selector in Table S2. These substantially broaden actual comparisons beyond the retained main-table baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds controlled prefilter comparisons, coverage-only selection, DA-v3 extrapolated-view configurations, and residual-sampling controls, including doubled sampling ratios for single-attribute variants. The extended main benchmark drops Barn and Francis, reducing seven scenes to five. The documented default reprojection threshold changes from 0.5 pixels to 1 pixel. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether coverage filtering beats alternative criteria, whether uncertainty adds value beyond coverage, and how residual supervision depends on the uncertain-Gaussian ratio and opacity/scale ranking (Tables S2–S4). DA-v3 alignment and extrapolated-view analyses replace the pi3 backbone study. The existing correspondence-noise, reprojection-threshold, hash-size, and selected-view-count studies are retained and reorganized.

E5.justification: v1 already reports four-seed main results with uncertainty values, despite an inconsistent single-run, seed-0 statement in Appendix A.2. v3 explicitly identifies means and standard deviations and extends four-run reporting to component ablations in Tables S13–S14. It removes the single-run statement and the five-run runtime disclosure. This establishes changed reporting, not a general increase in run counts.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive DA-v3, baseline, controlled-ablation, and scene-wise results while retaining the default main NeRF Synthetic and Mip-NeRF 360 scores. Component-ablation summaries change, and Truck LPIPS is corrected from 0.002 to 0.403 (v1 Table S8; v3 Table S12). Extended-benchmark PSNR changes from 20.060 to 20.401 under different scene subsets, not a comparable performance gain. End-to-end runtime savings are corrected from 55% to 40% with unchanged absolute times.

T1.justification: v1 motivates residual supervision through a qualitative dropout/ResNet analogy. v3 Section 3.3 adds an explicit alpha-compositing gradient derivation, including the transmittance factor 1/(1-alpha_k) after masking a preceding Gaussian (Equation 7). This is a focused mathematical addition; the original core method equations remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three central contributions: physically grounded view selection, residual supervision for weakly contributing Gaussians, and implicitly debiased uncertainty estimation. The skip-connection wording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of DA-v3 alignment ambiguity, residual-gradient amplification, and the interpretation of larger run-to-run variance as occasional performance gains (Appendices A.5 and I). It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning moving objects, illumination changes, and hyperparameter dependence, alongside the pi3 alignment-drift discussion. The account of mechanisms and applicability therefore changes substantially.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the DA-v3 checkpoint, alignment procedure, confidence threshold, and input configuration; clarifies that SA-Points do not enter initialization; and adds a project-page address. Conversely, it replaces the explicit V100/32-GB specification with a generic 38-TFLOPS GPU description and removes pi3 implementation details. Most default-pipeline implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands to discuss PRIMU and newer uncertainty applications, with additional references for DA-v3, ActiveNeRF, Umeyama alignment, MUSIQ, and CrossScore; the pi3 reference disappears. The central positioning as an extension of FisherRF combining geometric coverage and targeted residual supervision remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, related work, method explanation, and experimental discussion are rewritten. The supplement is reorganized into separate sections for prefiltering ablations, residual-learning ablations, robustness, additional baselines, and statistics. Terminology, cross-references, and author information are also revised, constituting extensive editorial restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 2, adds a DA-v3 alignment figure, redisplays existing camera-distribution evidence in main-text Figure 6, and annotates the uncertainty figure with AUSE values. Table 1 consolidates dataset subtables, Table 2 combines main and supplementary ablations, and new analysis/statistics tables are introduced. The document layout changes extensively, while most qualitative comparisons are retained.

improvement.justification: The controlled prefiltering and residual-sampling studies make central design choices more assessable, supported by the new gradient derivation and four-run ablation statistics. Corrections to runtime savings and numerical reporting also improve accuracy. These provide a limited net improvement, tempered by the unexplained removal of two extended-benchmark scenes, loss of explicit applicability limitations, and less specific hardware disclosure.
